extracted_stakeholders.name: Indonesian Government
extracted_stakeholders.role: Responsible for creating and enforcing policies and regulations regarding infrastructure development and forest conservation.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Private Sector Companies
extracted_stakeholders.role: Involved in the development and financing of infrastructure projects, particularly in construction and related industries.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Local and Indigenous Communities
extracted_stakeholders.role: Directly impacted by infrastructure projects through changes in livelihoods, displacement, and involvement in decision-making processes.

extracted_stakeholders.name: Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs)
extracted_stakeholders.role: Advocate for sustainable practices and environmental conservation; monitor deforestation and influence policy.

extracted_stakeholders.name: International Organizations
extracted_stakeholders.role: Provide funding, policy recommendations, and technical expertise to support sustainable infrastructure development.

extracted_factors.Label: Infrastructure Expansion
extracted_factors.Description: Infrastructure expansion, such as the construction of roads, railways, and ports, is a direct driver of deforestation in Indonesia, often facilitating access to remote areas and leading to land conversion.

extracted_factors.Label: Economic Growth Policies
extracted_factors.Description: National and regional policies aiming for economic growth often prioritize infrastructure development, which indirectly contributes to deforestation by promoting sectors with high deforestation footprints.

extracted_factors.Label: Population Dynamics
extracted_factors.Description: Population growth and urbanization increase demand for infrastructure, putting indirect pressure on forested areas and leading to deforestation.

extracted_factors.Label: Global Commodity Demand
extracted_factors.Description: International demand for commodities like palm oil and timber drives infrastructure projects to facilitate their transport, indirectly leading to deforestation.

extracted_factors.Label: Sustainability and Technology Adoption
extracted_factors.Description: The adoption of sustainable practices and technologies in infrastructure projects can mitigate environmental impacts and contribute to long-term forest conservation.

extracted_pain_points.description: Weak land tenure systems and governance issues lead to unregulated infrastructure expansion and deforestation.
Balancing economic growth objectives with environmental sustainability remains a key challenge in the context of infrastructure expansion.
Limited adoption and implementation of advanced monitoring and sustainable construction technologies complicate efforts to mitigate deforestation.
